dataset_description: This is the repository's processed version of the UCI Online News Popularity dataset (Fernandes, Vinagre, Cortez, and Sernadela, 2015; UCI dataset DOI 10.24432/C5NS3V), introduced in "A Proactive Intelligent Decision Support System for Predicting the Popularity of Online News" (paper DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-23485-4_53). The UCI source contains 39,797 Mashable articles collected over roughly two years, from January 7, 2013 through January 7, 2015, and was acquired on January 8, 2015. Because Mashable retains the article-content rights, the source distributes URLs and extracted statistics rather than the article text. The paper defines popularity using Mashable's total shares across Facebook, Twitter, Google+, LinkedIn, StumbleUpon, and Pinterest. This processed table has 38,458 rows and 54 columns: 53 inputs and the binary target is_popular. Preprocessing drops url and raw shares, collapses seven weekday flags into week_day, removes 1,186 rows for which both non-neutral sentiment rates are zero, and defines is_popular as 1 when shares >= 1,400 and 0 otherwise. The eight categorical inputs are six binary Mashable data-channel indicators, week_day, and is_weekend; is_popular is also categorical. The six channel flags cover lifestyle, entertainment, business, social media, tech, and world, are mutually exclusive when active, and may all be zero when none of those six channels applies (the paper also identifies viral as a possible Mashable category). week_day is one of monday through sunday, and is_weekend equals 1 exactly for saturday or sunday. The other 45 inputs are numerical. timedelta is retained even though UCI labels it non-predictive. Important exact or semantic relationships in this processed table are: num_self_hrefs <= num_hrefs; self_reference_min_shares <= self_reference_avg_sharess <= self_reference_max_shares; each keyword triplet is ordered minimum <= average <= maximum; the five LDA values sum to 1; rate_positive_words + rate_negative_words = 1 after the zero-rate rows are removed; abs_title_subjectivity = abs(title_subjectivity - 0.5); and abs_title_sentiment_polarity = abs(title_sentiment_polarity). UCI reports no missing values in the source, and preprocessing preserves that property.

column_descriptions.timedelta: Elapsed whole days from the article's publication date to the dataset acquisition date (January 8, 2015). UCI designates this as a non-predictive field; it records article age at acquisition rather than an intrinsic content property.
column_descriptions.n_tokens_title: Number of word tokens in the article title.
column_descriptions.n_tokens_content: Number of word tokens in the article body.
column_descriptions.n_unique_tokens: Proportion of article-body word tokens that are unique.
column_descriptions.n_non_stop_words: Proportion of article-body word tokens that are not stop words.
column_descriptions.n_non_stop_unique_tokens: Proportion of non-stop-word tokens in the article body that are unique.
column_descriptions.num_hrefs: Total number of hyperlinks in the article.
column_descriptions.num_self_hrefs: Number of hyperlinks from the article to other Mashable articles. These self-references are included in num_hrefs, so num_self_hrefs cannot exceed num_hrefs.
column_descriptions.num_imgs: Number of images embedded in the article.
column_descriptions.num_videos: Number of videos embedded in the article.
column_descriptions.average_token_length: Mean length of the word tokens in the article body, measured in characters per token.
column_descriptions.num_keywords: Number of keywords assigned in the article metadata.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_lifestyle: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the Lifestyle channel and 0 otherwise. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1; all six may be 0 for another or unrepresented channel.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_entertainment: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the Entertainment channel and 0 otherwise. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1; all six may be 0 for another or unrepresented channel.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_bus: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the Business channel and 0 otherwise. The abbreviated suffix 'bus' is inherited from the source schema. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_socmed: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the Social Media channel and 0 otherwise. The abbreviated suffix 'socmed' is inherited from the source schema. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_tech: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the Tech channel and 0 otherwise. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1; all six may be 0 for another or unrepresented channel.
column_descriptions.data_channel_is_world: Binary Mashable data-channel indicator: 1 when the article belongs to the World channel and 0 otherwise. At most one of the six retained data_channel_is_* indicators is 1; all six may be 0 for another or unrepresented channel.
column_descriptions.kw_min_min: Minimum historical share count for the article's worst-performing keyword. Worst, middle, and best keywords are ranked using their average shares in Mashable articles published before the current article.
column_descriptions.kw_max_min: Maximum historical share count for the article's worst-performing keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_avg_min: Mean historical share count for the article's worst-performing keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_min_max: Minimum historical share count for the article's best-performing keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_max_max: Maximum historical share count for the article's best-performing keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_avg_max: Mean historical share count for the article's best-performing keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_min_avg: Minimum historical share count for the article's middle, or average-performing, keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_max_avg: Maximum historical share count for the article's middle, or average-performing, keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.kw_avg_avg: Mean historical share count for the article's middle, or average-performing, keyword, where keyword rank is based on average shares before publication.
column_descriptions.self_reference_min_shares: Minimum Mashable share count among the earlier Mashable articles linked from the current article; these counts were known before the current article was published.
column_descriptions.self_reference_max_shares: Maximum Mashable share count among the earlier Mashable articles linked from the current article; these counts were known before the current article was published.
column_descriptions.self_reference_avg_sharess: Mean Mashable share count among the earlier Mashable articles linked from the current article; these counts were known before the current article was published. The misspelling 'sharess' is inherited from the source schema.
column_descriptions.week_day: Nominal publication weekday derived by collapsing the source's seven weekday indicator columns. Its value is one of monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, or sunday.
column_descriptions.is_weekend: Binary publication-day indicator: 1 exactly when week_day is saturday or sunday, and 0 from monday through friday.
column_descriptions.LDA_00: Article's membership weight for latent Dirichlet allocation topic 0. LDA was applied to Mashable article text to identify five topics; the five LDA_00 through LDA_04 weights are nonnegative and sum to 1.
column_descriptions.LDA_01: Article's membership weight for latent Dirichlet allocation topic 1. Together, LDA_00 through LDA_04 form a five-topic probability distribution and sum to 1.
column_descriptions.LDA_02: Article's membership weight for latent Dirichlet allocation topic 2. Together, LDA_00 through LDA_04 form a five-topic probability distribution and sum to 1.
column_descriptions.LDA_03: Article's membership weight for latent Dirichlet allocation topic 3. Together, LDA_00 through LDA_04 form a five-topic probability distribution and sum to 1.
column_descriptions.LDA_04: Article's membership weight for latent Dirichlet allocation topic 4. Together, LDA_00 through LDA_04 form a five-topic probability distribution and sum to 1.
column_descriptions.global_subjectivity: Pattern sentiment-analysis subjectivity score for the article body, on a 0-to-1 scale where 0 is objective and 1 is subjective.
column_descriptions.global_sentiment_polarity: Pattern sentiment-analysis polarity score for the article body. Negative values indicate negative sentiment, 0 is neutral, and positive values indicate positive sentiment.
column_descriptions.global_rate_positive_words: Number of positive-polarity words divided by the total number of word tokens in the article body.
column_descriptions.global_rate_negative_words: Number of negative-polarity words divided by the total number of word tokens in the article body.
column_descriptions.rate_positive_words: Fraction of sentiment-bearing (positive or negative) words that are positive. This value plus rate_negative_words equals 1.
column_descriptions.rate_negative_words: Fraction of sentiment-bearing (positive or negative) words that are negative. This value plus rate_positive_words equals 1.
column_descriptions.avg_positive_polarity: Mean sentiment-polarity score among positive words in the article body. It lies between min_positive_polarity and max_positive_polarity.
column_descriptions.min_positive_polarity: Minimum sentiment-polarity score among positive words in the article body; this is the positive word score closest to neutral.
column_descriptions.max_positive_polarity: Maximum sentiment-polarity score among positive words in the article body; this is the most strongly positive word score.
column_descriptions.avg_negative_polarity: Mean sentiment-polarity score among negative words in the article body. Because negative polarity uses signed values, it lies between min_negative_polarity and max_negative_polarity.
column_descriptions.min_negative_polarity: Minimum sentiment-polarity score among negative words in the article body; on the signed polarity scale, this is the most strongly negative value.
column_descriptions.max_negative_polarity: Maximum sentiment-polarity score among negative words in the article body; on the signed polarity scale, this is the negative value closest to neutral.
column_descriptions.title_subjectivity: Pattern sentiment-analysis subjectivity score for the article title, on a 0-to-1 scale where 0 is objective and 1 is subjective.
column_descriptions.title_sentiment_polarity: Pattern sentiment-analysis polarity score for the article title, ranging from negative sentiment through 0 (neutral) to positive sentiment.
column_descriptions.abs_title_subjectivity: Absolute distance of title_subjectivity from the neutral midpoint 0.5: abs(title_subjectivity - 0.5). Its range is 0 to 0.5; it is not simply abs(title_subjectivity).
column_descriptions.abs_title_sentiment_polarity: Magnitude of the title sentiment-polarity score: abs(title_sentiment_polarity). It discards sentiment direction and retains strength.
column_descriptions.is_popular: Binary classification target derived from the removed shares field: 1 when the article received at least 1,400 Mashable shares and 0 when it received fewer than 1,400. This repository uses >= 1,400 for the positive class.
